interpretation.execution: The v0.14 physical typed-array invariant survives: incremental ArrayBuffer peak above the already-loaded pre-run system is exactly 39,820 B in all five samples.
interpretation.state: The persistent 2,500-file JavaScript truth fixture adds about 1.64 MB heapUsed at creation in this process shape; dropping the canonical state later recovers about 1.44 MB heapUsed median.
interpretation.fingerprint: The state-fingerprint stage expands RSS and heapTotal while post-GC heapUsed falls. This is an observed high-water/capacity effect, not evidence that the retained fingerprint string itself costs 5.8 MB. The exact temporary allocation/heap-growth cause is not yet isolated.
interpretation.rss: After result, state, session, and registry references are dropped, RSS remains about 15.64 MB above the original module-loaded boot snapshot while ArrayBuffer returns fully to baseline. This is a process/runtime high-water observation, not live capability-body memory and not proof those pages are irreclaimable by the OS.
interpretation.fleet: The active capability body is no longer the dominant memory envelope in this Node fixture. Any datacenter-scale savings claim would require amortizing or otherwise reducing runtime/process/state overhead and testing real concurrent services; v0.15 does not establish fleet savings.

truthBoundary: RSS, heapTotal, heapUsed, external, ArrayBuffer, and V8 malloced memory overlap and are not additive buckets.
Forced GC checkpoints do not guarantee immediate RSS return to the operating system.
The Node/module boot baseline is not attributed to individual capabilities.
The 2,500-file JavaScript fixture is not a universal canonical-state representation.
The fingerprint-stage RSS/heapTotal expansion has not yet been isolated to a specific line-level allocation mechanism.
No datacenter, container-density, energy, CPU, cloud-cost, or fleet-level savings claim is established.
nextGate: Isolate v0.15's fingerprint-stage high-water. Compare current stableStringify(value) -> fnv1a32(text), which materializes a complete canonical serialization string, against a deterministic streaming/incremental FNV path that emits the exact same hash without retaining the whole serialization at once. Measure heapUsed, heapTotal, RSS high-water, timing, exact hash equivalence, and counterexamples.
